question: Who ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 A.D. as the only woman monarch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Razia Sultana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Razia Sultana (रज़िया सुल्तान) ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 A.D. and was the only woman ever to sit on the throne of Delhi.

• She was the daughter of Iltutmish, the Slave/Mamluk dynasty ruler, who nominated her as his successor over his sons.

• She discarded the veil, held open court and appointed Jamal-ud-din Yaqut to a high post, which angered the Turkish nobles (the Chahalgani/Forty).

• She was overthrown and killed in 1240 A.D.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Razia belonged to the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

• Iltutmish was the first ruler to introduce the silver coin tanka and the copper coin jital.

• The Slave Dynasty ruled Delhi from 1206 to 1290 A.D.

NOTE

• Noor Jahan (Option 1): Mughal empress, wife of Emperor Jahangir, known for her strong influence in Mughal administration.

• Rani Durgavati (Option 3): Gond queen of Garha-Katanga who fought the Mughals under Akbar in 1564.

• Chand Bibi (Option 4): Regent of Ahmadnagar who defended the fort against Akbar's Mughal army.

question: What was the total number of Alvar saints in the Bhakti movement tradition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Alvars (आलवार संत) were a group of 12 Vaishnava saint-poets of South India who were devoted to Lord Vishnu.

• Their devotional hymns are compiled in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham (4000 verses).

• They flourished mainly in the Tamil region between the 6th and 9th centuries A.D.

• The word 'Alvar' means 'one who is immersed' in the love of God.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The counterpart Shaivite saints devoted to Lord Shiva were the 63 Nayanars.

• Andal was the only woman among the 12 Alvars.

• The Bhakti movement emphasised devotion (bhakti) as the path to salvation, rejecting ritualism and caste barriers.

NOTE

• 29 (Option 2): Not associated with the count of Alvar saints.

• 44 (Option 3): Not associated with the count of Alvar saints.

• 63 (Option 4): This is the number of Nayanar saints (devotees of Shiva), not the Alvars.

question: Which of the following article of the Indian constitution is related with the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 30 (अनुच्छेद 30) grants minorities (religious or linguistic) the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

• It falls under the Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30) of the Fundamental Rights.

• The State cannot discriminate against any educational institution while granting aid on the ground that it is managed by a minority.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution.

• Article 29 protects the interests of minorities by allowing them to conserve their distinct language, script or culture.

• These rights aim to preserve the diversity and heritage of minority communities.

NOTE

• Article 28 (Option 1): Deals with freedom regarding attendance at religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

• Article 24 (Option 2): Prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or hazardous work.

• Article 29 (Option 4): Protects the right of any section of citizens to conserve their distinct language, script or culture.

question: Sanjiv Ranjan assumed the role of secretary general of the which of the following organisation on January 1, 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IORA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian diplomat Sanjiv Ranjan assumed charge as the Secretary General of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) (हिंद महासागर तटीय संघ) on January 1, 2025.

• IORA is an inter-governmental organisation established in 1997 to promote regional cooperation among Indian Ocean rim states.

• Its headquarters (Secretariat) is located in Ebene, Mauritius.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• IORA currently has 23 member states and several dialogue partners.

• Its guiding principles are open regionalism and consensus-based decision making.

• India is a founding member of IORA.

NOTE

• SAARC (Option 2): South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, founded 1985, headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal.

• ASEAN (Option 3): Association of Southeast Asian Nations, founded 1967, headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia.

• BRICS (Option 4): Grouping of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and newer members; a major economic bloc.

question: The nickname "Flying Sikh" is associated with which Indian athlete?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milkha Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh (मिल्खा सिंह) was nicknamed the "Flying Sikh" (उड़न सिख).

• The title was reportedly given to him by Pakistan's President Field Marshal Ayub Khan after a race in Pakistan.

• He won gold medals in the 1958 and 1962 Asian Games and the 1958 Commonwealth Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He narrowly missed a bronze at the 1960 Rome Olympics in the 400 m, finishing fourth.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1959.

• His autobiography 'The Race of My Life' inspired the biopic 'Bhaag Milkha Bhaag'.

NOTE

• Avinash Sable (Option 1): Indian long-distance runner and national record holder in the 3000 m steeplechase.

• Vikas Gowda (Option 3): Indian discus thrower and Olympian.

• Harbhajan Singh (Option 4): Former Indian cricketer, an off-spin bowler.

question: In May 2025, who has been given one-year extension as the Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Secretary of the Department of Defence Research and Development (DDR&D) from India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Samir V. Kamat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Samir V. Kamat (डॉ. समीर वी. कामत) was given a one-year extension in May 2025 as the Chairman of DRDO and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D (DDR&D).

• DRDO is the premier agency under the Ministry of Defence for military research and development.

• It was established in 1958 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• DRDO's motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (The root of strength is science).

• DRDO has developed missile systems such as Agni, Prithvi, Akash and BrahMos (with Russia).

• The DRDO Bhavan is located in New Delhi.

NOTE

• Dr. G. Satheesh Reddy (Option 1): Former DRDO Chairman and noted missile scientist.

• Dr. Ajay Kumar (Option 2): Former Defence Secretary of India.

• M N Srinivasu (Option 4): Not associated with the DRDO chairmanship extension in this context.

question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, a Maritime Development Fund of Rs. ______ crore over 10 years has been announced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26, a Maritime Development Fund (समुद्री विकास कोष) of Rs. 25,000 crore was announced to be deployed over 10 years.

• The fund aims to boost the shipbuilding and maritime sector and provide long-term financing.

• Up to 49% of the fund is to be contributed by the government, with the balance mobilised from ports and the private sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

• It also expanded the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy and introduced Shipbuilding Clusters.

• The maritime push aligns with the Maritime India Vision 2030 and Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

NOTE

• 20000 (Option 1): Not the announced corpus of the Maritime Development Fund.

• 30000 (Option 3): Not the announced corpus of the Maritime Development Fund.

• 35000 (Option 4): Not the announced corpus of the Maritime Development Fund.

question: Which organisation published the Multidimensional Vulnerability Index?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Nations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI) (बहुआयामी सुभेद्यता सूचकांक) was developed and published by the United Nations (संयुक्त राष्ट्र).

• It was designed particularly to assess the structural vulnerability of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and other developing countries.

• It looks beyond income (GNI per capita) to capture vulnerability to economic, environmental and social shocks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A UN High-Level Panel was set up to develop the MVI.

• The index helps determine access to concessional finance for vulnerable nations.

• The UN headquarters is located in New York, USA.

NOTE

• World Bank (Option 2): Publishes reports such as the World Development Report and Ease of Doing Business (discontinued).

• NITI Aayog (Option 3): India's policy think tank; publishes the SDG India Index and Multidimensional Poverty Index (India).

• IMF (Option 4): International Monetary Fund; publishes the World Economic Outlook.

question: NTPC, India's largest power producer, inaugurated the world's first CO2-to-methanol conversion plant at its ______ facility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vindhyachal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NTPC inaugurated the world's first CO2-to-methanol conversion plant at its Vindhyachal (विंध्याचल) facility in Madhya Pradesh.

• The plant captures carbon dioxide from flue gases and converts it into methanol, supporting carbon capture and utilisation.

• Vindhyachal is NTPC's largest thermal power station in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NTPC Limited was founded in 1975 and is a Maharatna public sector undertaking.

• Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

• The initiative supports India's goal of net-zero emissions by 2070.

NOTE

• Chittor (Option 2): A historic city in Rajasthan known for Chittorgarh Fort, not this NTPC plant.

• Ranchi (Option 3): Capital of Jharkhand; not the site of this plant.

• Kolkata (Option 4): Capital of West Bengal; not the site of this plant.

question: Which among the following is a book authored by Arundhati Roy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Capitalism- A Ghost Story.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Capitalism: A Ghost Story' (कैपिटलिज्म – ए घोस्ट स्टोरी) is a non-fiction book written by Arundhati Roy.

• Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for her debut novel 'The God of Small Things'.

• She is also known for her novel 'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' and several essay collections.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Arundhati Roy is well known as an author and political activist.

• 'Capitalism: A Ghost Story' critiques corporate power and inequality in India.

• She was awarded the Booker Prize as the first Indian woman to win it.

NOTE

• Flood of Fire (Option 1): A novel by Amitav Ghosh, the final part of his Ibis trilogy.

• The Circle of Reason (Option 2): The debut novel of Amitav Ghosh.

• The Liberation of Sita (Option 4): A work by Telugu writer Volga (P. Lalita Kumari).

question: Who is the author of the book 'Shalimar The Clown'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salman Rushdie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Shalimar the Clown' is a novel written by Salman Rushdie (सलमान रुश्दी), published in 2005.

• The novel is set largely in Kashmir and deals with themes of terrorism, love and revenge.

• Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize (1981) for his novel 'Midnight's Children'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 'Midnight's Children' also won the Booker of Bookers.

• His controversial novel 'The Satanic Verses' led to a fatwa against him.

• Other works include 'Haroun and the Sea of Stories' and 'The Moor's Last Sigh'.

NOTE

• Anita Desai (Option 1): Indian novelist known for 'Fasting, Feasting' and 'Clear Light of Day'.

• Shiva Naipaul (Option 2): Trinidadian writer, younger brother of V. S. Naipaul.

• Rohinton Mistry (Option 4): Indian-Canadian author of 'A Fine Balance' and 'Such a Long Journey'.

question: The Indus Valley people used standardized ______ as a building material.
solution_text:
The correct answer is burnt mud-bricks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The people of the Indus Valley Civilisation used standardized burnt (baked) mud-bricks (पकाई गई ईंटें) as their principal building material.

• The bricks followed a fixed ratio of 4:2:1 (length:breadth:height), showing remarkable uniformity.

• The extensive use of kiln-baked bricks distinguished the Harappan cities from contemporary civilisations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Indus Valley Civilisation is also called the Harappan Civilisation (c. 2500 BCE).

• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal and Kalibangan.

• The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is a famous example of their brick engineering.

NOTE

• rocks (Option 2): Not the standardized building material of the Harappans, who relied on bricks.

• fly ash (Option 3): A modern by-product of coal combustion used in present-day construction.

• black soil (Option 4): A cotton-growing soil (regur), not a standardized building material of the Indus Valley.

question: The 'Veerampattinam Festival' is celebrated in which Indian state/UT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Veerampattinam Festival (वीरमपट्टिनम महोत्सव) is celebrated in the Union Territory of Puducherry (पुद्दुचेरी).

• It is a famous car (chariot) festival held at the coastal village of Veerampattinam near Puducherry.

• The festival is dedicated to the local deity Sri Thirumbadi Amman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Puducherry is a Union Territory with a former French colonial heritage.

• It comprises four regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.

• Puducherry has a Legislative Assembly and a Lieutenant Governor.

NOTE

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for festivals like Onam and Thrissur Pooram.

• Telangana (Option 3): Known for the Bathukamma and Bonalu festivals.

• Lakshadweep (Option 4): An island Union Territory in the Arabian Sea.

question: In the context of Indian satellite launch vehicle, what does "G" stands for in GSLV?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geosynchronous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In GSLV, the letter "G" stands for Geosynchronous (जियोसिंक्रोनस) — the full form is Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle.

• GSLV is used by ISRO to place satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).

• It is a heavier launch vehicle than the PSLV and carries a cryogenic upper stage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• GSLV Mk III (LVM3) is India's heaviest launcher, used for Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3 and Gaganyaan.

• ISRO was established in 1969 and is headquartered in Bengaluru.

• PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle.

NOTE

• Gladiator (Option 2): Not the expansion of 'G' in GSLV.

• Gentle (Option 3): Not the expansion of 'G' in GSLV.

• Generation (Option 4): Not the expansion of 'G' in GSLV.

question: The magnitude of buoyant force depends on the ______ of the fluid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is density.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The magnitude of the buoyant force (उत्प्लावन बल) depends on the density (घनत्व) of the fluid (along with the volume displaced and gravity).

• By Archimedes' principle, buoyant force = weight of the fluid displaced = density × volume × g.

• A denser fluid exerts a greater upward buoyant force on a submerged object.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• This is why objects float more easily in sea water (denser) than in fresh water.

• Buoyant force acts vertically upward through the centre of buoyancy.

• Archimedes was the Greek scientist who formulated this principle.

NOTE

• refractive index (Option 1): An optical property that measures how light bends in a medium; unrelated to buoyancy.

• colour (Option 3): A visual property that does not affect the buoyant force.

• charge (Option 4): An electrical property, not a factor in the buoyant force of a fluid.

question: What was the combined army of the Sikh 'Jathas' and 'Misls' called in the eighteenth century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dal Khalsa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The combined army of the Sikh Jathas and Misls in the eighteenth century was called the Dal Khalsa (दल खालसा).

• It was organised at Amritsar to unite the scattered Sikh fighting bands against foreign invaders and the Mughals.

• The Dal Khalsa was later divided into the Budha Dal (army of veterans) and the Taruna Dal (army of the young).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A Misl was an autonomous Sikh confederacy; there were about 12 Misls.

• Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl later unified the Sikhs into a powerful empire.

• The Sikh Empire had its capital at Lahore.

NOTE

• Sangats (Option 1): Congregations or communities of Sikh devotees, not a military force.

• Mansabdars (Option 2): Holders of military-administrative ranks (mansabs) in the Mughal administration.

• Nihangs (Option 3): An armed Sikh warrior order known for their blue robes and martial traditions.

question: Personal Disposable Income is the part of the aggregate income which belongs to the ______
solution_text:
The correct answer is households.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Personal Disposable Income (वैयक्तिक प्रयोज्य आय) is the part of the aggregate income which belongs to the households (घरेलू क्षेत्र) and is at their disposal.

• It is the income available to households after paying direct taxes and non-tax obligations.

• Formula: Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − Direct Taxes − Miscellaneous receipts of the government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Disposable income is used by households for consumption and saving.

• Personal Income = Private Income − Undistributed Profits − Corporate Tax.

• National income accounting concepts are widely tested in SSC exams.

NOTE

• firm (Option 2): A production unit; its earnings are counted as profits, not personal disposable income.

• government (Option 3): The public authority that collects taxes; income here is not personal disposable income.

• foreign banks (Option 4): External financial institutions, not the recipients of personal disposable income.

question: Tantia Tope was the general of whom among the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nana Saheb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tantia Tope (तात्या टोपे) was the trusted general (सेनापति) of Nana Saheb during the Revolt of 1857.

• He led the rebellion in the Kanpur (Cawnpore) region and was a brilliant guerrilla commander.

• He later joined Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi in the fight against the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tantia Tope was captured and executed by the British in 1859.

• Nana Saheb was the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II and led the revolt at Kanpur.

• The Revolt of 1857 is also called the First War of Indian Independence.

NOTE

• Begum Hazrat Mahal (Option 2): Led the 1857 revolt in Lucknow (Awadh).

• Bahadur Shah Zafar (Option 3): The last Mughal emperor, declared the symbolic leader of the 1857 revolt.

• Baji Rao I (Option 4): A celebrated Maratha Peshwa (1720-1740), not linked with Tantia Tope.

question: In India, projects having a minimum investment of Rs. ______ Crore in plant & machinery shall be considered for establishment as EOUs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, projects having a minimum investment of Rs. 1 crore in plant and machinery are considered for establishment as Export Oriented Units (EOUs) (निर्यात उन्मुख इकाइयाँ).

• EOUs are units that undertake to export their entire production of goods and services (with permitted exceptions).

• The EOU Scheme was introduced in 1981 to boost exports and earn foreign exchange.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• EOUs can be set up for manufacturing, services, agriculture, aquaculture and similar activities.

• The scheme is administered under the Foreign Trade Policy by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

• EOUs enjoy various duty and tax benefits on imports and domestic procurement.

NOTE

• 5 (Option 1): Not the prescribed minimum investment threshold for an EOU.

• 10 (Option 2): Not the prescribed minimum investment threshold for an EOU.

• 3 (Option 4): Not the prescribed minimum investment threshold for an EOU.

question: A Bill passed by the Indian State Legislature is sent to the Governor under ______
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 200.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 200 (अनुच्छेद 200), a Bill passed by the State Legislature is presented to the Governor for assent.

• The Governor may give assent, withhold assent, return the Bill (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or reserve it for the consideration of the President.

• If the Bill is passed again by the legislature, the Governor must give assent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 201 deals with Bills reserved by the Governor for the President's consideration.

• Articles 168-212 (Part VI) deal with the State Legislature.

• The Governor is the constitutional head of the State.

NOTE

• Article 201 (Option 2): Deals with Bills reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President.

• Article 202 (Option 3): Deals with the Annual Financial Statement (State Budget).

• Article 203 (Option 4): Deals with the procedure in the legislature with respect to estimates.

question: Which of the following port is situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marmagao port.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Marmagao (Mormugao) port (मर्मागाओ बंदरगाह) is situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary in Goa.

• It is a natural harbour on the west coast of India and a leading iron-ore exporting port.

• It is one of India's major ports administered under the central government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Marmagao serves as the principal port of the state of Goa.

• It lies on the Arabian Sea coast.

• India has 13 major ports (12 government-administered plus Vadhavan/others as notified).

NOTE

• Mumbai port (Option 1): A major natural harbour on the west coast in Maharashtra.

• Haldia port (Option 3): A riverine port on the Hooghly river in West Bengal, part of Kolkata Port Trust.

• Paradip port (Option 4): A major port on the east coast in Odisha at the mouth of the Mahanadi delta.

question: The ninth five year plan of India was launched in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ninth Five Year Plan (नौवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना) of India covered the period 1997 to 2002.

• Its main theme was 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity'.

• It was launched in the 50th year of India's independence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Five Year Plans were formulated by the Planning Commission, set up in 1950.

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

NOTE

• 1985 (Option 1): Year the Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90) began.

• 1992 (Option 2): Year the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) began.

• 2003 (Option 4): Falls within the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) period.

question:
When do desert plants typically take up carbon dioxide?
I. During the day
II. During the night
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Desert plants (like cacti) typically take up carbon dioxide during the night (रात्रि के दौरान), so the correct statement is Only II.

• They follow the CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) pathway of photosynthesis.

• Opening their stomata at night (when it is cooler) minimises water loss through transpiration in the hot desert climate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• At night, CO2 is fixed and stored as malic acid in vacuoles.

• During the day, the stored CO2 is released for the Calvin cycle while the stomata remain closed.

• This adaptation makes CAM plants highly water-efficient.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as desert (CAM) plants keep their stomata closed during the day to conserve water.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, as CO2 uptake occurs mainly at night, not during the day.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as desert plants do take up CO2 at night.

question: Which of the following part of brain is responsible for the precision of voluntary actions and maintaining the posture and balance of the body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cerebellum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cerebellum (अनुमस्तिष्क) is responsible for the precision of voluntary actions and for maintaining posture and balance of the body.

• It coordinates muscular activity and ensures smooth, well-timed movements.

• It is located in the hindbrain, below the cerebrum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The human brain has three main parts: forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.

• The hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, pons and medulla oblongata.

• Damage to the cerebellum can cause loss of balance and unsteady movements (ataxia).

NOTE

• Cerebrum (Option 1): The largest part of the brain, controlling thinking, memory, intelligence and voluntary actions.

• Medulla (Option 3): The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure.

• Hypothalamus (Option 4): Regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst and links the nervous and endocrine systems.

question: Samudragupta celebrated his conquests by performing which Vedic sacrifice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashvamedha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Samudragupta celebrated his military conquests by performing the Ashvamedha (अश्वमेध) sacrifice (the horse sacrifice).

• He issued special Ashvamedha-type gold coins to commemorate this event.

• His achievements are recorded in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti), composed by his court poet Harishena.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Samudragupta of the Gupta Dynasty is often called the 'Napoleon of India' (a title given by historian V. A. Smith).

• He was the son of Chandragupta I and a great patron of art and music.

• The Gupta period is regarded as the 'Golden Age of India'.

NOTE

• Shraddha (Option 1): A ritual performed in honour of one's ancestors, not a conquest sacrifice.

• Agnihotra (Option 2): A daily fire ritual (oblation into the sacred fire), not connected with celebrating conquests.

• Upanayana (Option 3): The sacred thread (initiation) ceremony marking the beginning of formal education.
